title: MECoBench: A Systematic Study of Multimodal Agent Collaboration in Embodied Environments
title_zh: MECoBench：具身环境中多模态智能体协作的系统研究
abstract_en: Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have strong potential as embodied agents, but their ability to collaborate in visually grounded environments remains underexplored. To address this gap, we introduce MECoBench, a multimodal embodied cooperation benchmark with an evaluation platform spanning diverse real-world tasks, two cooperation structures, and three collaboration modes. Through extensive experiments across various MLLMs, we summarize three key findings: (i) Collaboration generally improves embodied task completion, but its benefits depend on balancing collaborative gains against coordination complexity. (ii) Communication is essential to collaboration gains, while the best collaboration mode depends on team size and model capability. (iii) Moreover, collaboration improves robustness under noisy priors and exploration conditions. Generally, MECoBench provides a systematic testbed for understanding the mechanisms and limits of multimodal embodied collaboration. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/q-i-n-g/MECoBench.
abstract_zh: 近期多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）展现出作为具身智能体的潜力，但其在视觉接地环境中的协作能力仍缺乏系统研究。本文提出 MECoBench，一个多模态具身协作基准与评测平台，覆盖多样化真实世界任务、两类协作结构和三种协作模式。作者在多种 MLLMs 上进行大量实验，总结出三点发现：协作通常能提升具身任务完成率，但收益取决于协作增益与协调复杂度之间的平衡；通信是获得协作收益的关键，而最佳协作模式受团队规模和模型能力影响；协作还能在先验噪声和探索不确定性条件下提升鲁棒性。总体而言，MECoBench 为理解多模态具身协作的机制与边界提供了系统化测试平台。
key_points_zh: 提出 MECoBench：面向多模态具身智能体协作的基准，覆盖真实世界任务、两类协作结构与三种协作模式。
实验证明协作通常提升任务完成表现，但团队协作带来的收益会受到协调复杂度的制约。
通信是协作性能提升的核心因素；不同团队规模和 MLLM 能力水平下，最优协作模式并不相同。
在存在噪声先验或探索不确定性的环境中，协作可增强具身智能体的鲁棒性。
该基准为研究视觉接地环境中多模态智能体协作的机制、限制与模型差异提供了统一评测平台。

llm_assessment.comment: A useful embodied multimodal-agent collaboration benchmark with reusable evaluation value, though it has limited emphasis on realtime voice/video interaction or latency-aware agent design.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 这是一个有用的具身多模态智能体协作基准，具备可复用评测价值，但对实时语音/视频交互和低延迟系统设计关注有限。
